articles.title: Scientists uncover how early life stress rewires the brain
articles.summary: Experiences in early life can alter how DNA is packaged inside brain cells. By artificially adding these molecular bookmarks to young mice, researchers successfully programmed a lifelong vulnerability to stress.

articles.title: This simple habit is linked to a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's
articles.summary: Reading for pleasure may have surprisingly powerful benefits for the brain, with studies linking it to better memory, reduced stress, improved mental health, and a lower risk of dementia. Researchers highlight findings that just five minutes of fiction can reduce stress by up to 20%, while reading has also been associated with a 33% lower risk of Alzheimer's disease.

articles.title: New psychology research sheds light on why certain pop song hooks stick in your head
articles.summary: New research in Psychology of Music indicates that repeated listening makes unfamiliar pop hooks feel more memorable, while verbal distraction dulls them. The findings offer clues into how earworms take hold.

articles.title: What two decades of psychology and neuroscience research say about playing Grand Theft Auto

articles.title: For better mental health, how often you exercise may matter more than how hard
articles.summary: A study of more than 10,000 college students found that exercising regularly may be more important for mental health than pushing yourself through intense or lengthy workouts. Students who exercised less frequently were more likely to experience depression and anxiety a year later, suggesting that consistency could be a key ingredient in protecting mental well-being.

articles.title: Acceptance and commitment therapy linked to neural shifts in the depressed brain
articles.summary: An eight-week therapeutic program aimed at improving psychological flexibility helped patients with depression reduce obsessive rumination. Brain scans show the therapy strengthened neural connectivity in regions responsible for emotional regulation.

articles.title: Neuroimaging study links heightened sensitivity to peer rejection with harsher parenting after childhood abuse
articles.summary: Why does childhood abuse carry over into harsh parenting in some families but not others? New fMRI findings indicate the connection holds only when a mother's brain reacts more strongly to negative than positive social feedback.

articles.title: Reanalysis of 1950s LSD experiments challenges the idea that psychedelics make art more creative

articles.title: Insecticide exposure in pregnancy linked to cognition in middle childhood
articles.summary: Neonicotinoids are among the most common insecticides worldwide, given their low cost and high efficacy. Despite the well-documented effects of neonicotinoids on insects and the environment, their impact on humans remains less clear.

articles.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months
